title: Health Care Efficiency Through Flexibility Act
official_title: To amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to ensure the availability of appropriate collection types for quality reporting under the Medicare Shared Savings Program, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Vern Buchanan (R-FL) and passed the House by voice vote (no recorded roll call); the bill amends Medicare Shared Savings Program quality reporting and now awaits Senate consideration.
summary: Requires Medicare to keep several ways of reporting quality data available to the doctor-and-hospital groups (called ACOs) that take part in the Medicare Shared Savings Program. It also tells Medicare to run a test program letting some of those groups report quality measures digitally.
brief: Requires Medicare to keep specified quality-reporting methods available to ACOs and to run a digital reporting pilot for the Medicare Shared Savings Program.

top_lines.headline: What the Medicare Shared Savings Program Does
subs: Lets provider groups form ACOs to coordinate care for Medicare fee-for-service patients
ACOs that hit quality standards can share in the savings they generate
ACOs must report quality-of-care data in the form Medicare specifies

top_lines.headline: Required Reporting Methods
subs: For performance years 2025-2029, three collection types must stay available
Covers electronic clinical, MIPS clinical, and Medicare CQMs for ACOs
Data not deemed unrepresentative solely because one ACO participant couldn't collect it

top_lines.headline: Digital Reporting Pilot
subs: New pilot for performance years 2028-2032 using a digital collection type
Selected ACOs report only 2 Medicare-specified measures, waiving the rest
Public analysis and recommendations due by December 31, 2032

items.main: Names the Act the "Health Care Efficiency Through Flexibility Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Ensuring Availability of Appropriate Collection Types for Quality Reporting

items.main: Amends Section 1899(b)(3)(B) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395jjj(b)(3)(B)) to require, for performance years 2025 through 2029, that the Secretary keep three collection types available for each quality measure an ACO must report.
items.detail: The Medicare Shared Savings Program lets provider groups act as ACOs coordinating care for Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries and submit quality data the Secretary determines necessary. This section requires that Electronic Clinical Quality Measures, MIPS Clinical Quality Measures, and Medicare Clinical Quality Measures for ACOs (as described in 42 CFR 414.1305) all remain available for reporting.

items.main: Adds a data-completeness clarification: for performance years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, the Secretary may not treat an ACO's data as unrepresentative solely because it excludes data from one or more ACO participants.
items.detail: The exclusion is protected only if the submitted data otherwise meets the completeness requirements of 42 CFR 414.1340 (as applied under 42 CFR 425.512) and the ACO shows to the Secretary's satisfaction that the participant could not collect the data through the selected collection type. "ACO participant" takes the meaning in 42 CFR 425.20, and the Secretary may implement the clause by program instruction or otherwise.

sections.label: Section 3 — Pilot Program for Digital Quality Measure Reporting

items.main: Further amends Section 1899(b)(3)(B) to require the Secretary to establish a digital quality measure reporting pilot program for each of performance years 2028 through 2032.
items.detail: The Secretary selects ACOs from among applicants; for each performance year the Secretary specifies 2 measures the selected ACOs report through a digital quality measure collection type, and may not require them to report other measures. Data for those measures is not counted toward quality performance standards or an ACO participant's quality performance category score, and the Secretary provides technical assistance as practicable.

items.main: Requires the Secretary, not later than December 31, 2032, to publicly post (or include in annual rulemaking) an analysis of the pilot and related recommendations.
items.detail: The posting must include recommendations for increasing submissions through the digital collection type and a proposed timeline for eventually requiring measures to be submitted through it.

underreported.summary: Data an ACO submits for the pilot's specified measures, and any measures it is relieved from reporting, are not taken into account in judging whether the ACO met quality performance standards or in a participant's quality performance category score.
underreported.why_unreported: The section is labeled a reporting pilot, but this provision means a participating ACO's pilot-year quality results carry no consequence for its quality-standard determinations.

gaps: The bill requires three collection types be available for performance years 2025-2029 but does not specify what collection types must be available after 2029.
The bill establishes a digital reporting pilot through 2032 but does not set criteria for how the Secretary selects participating ACOs beyond requiring an application.
The bill directs a proposed timeline for eventually requiring digital submission but does not itself set any deadline for making digital reporting mandatory.

added: New requirement that three collection types (eCQMs, MIPS CQMs, and Medicare CQMs for ACOs) remain available for ACO quality reporting for performance years 2025-2029
New data-completeness protection barring the Secretary from deeming ACO data unrepresentative solely for excluding a participant that could not collect through the selected collection type
New digital quality measure reporting pilot program for performance years 2028-2032, with a public analysis due by December 31, 2032
modified: Amends Section 1899(b)(3)(B) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395jjj(b)(3)(B)) to restructure the ACO reporting-requirements clause and add the collection-type, data-completeness, and pilot provisions
